source.title: Fractional moment-preserving initialization schemes for training deep neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares a new initialization method with established initializations and reports training metrics, bearing on initialization's effect on early training performance.
record.gate_note: The paper reports initialization comparisons and training outcomes. Many training curves are figure-only; rows below use numeric means and standard deviations stated in the text. The paper does not report training classification error near zero.
record.test_reason: The study compares initialization schemes under shared SGD stepsizes and reports early training accuracy and loss, directly testing V4's training-speed component. It does not establish V1's near-zero training error in sufficiently large convolutional networks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose fractional-moment-preserving initializations that generalize second-moment schemes and can improve early training. Their conclusion also emphasizes theoretical output-distribution and limiting results; it does not establish near-zero training error or greater maximum trainable depth.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes Gaussian weight initialization with variance chosen to preserve a fractional moment, then compares it with Kaiming, Xavier and, in some settings, random-walk initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset, activation, architecture, and initialization method; CIFAR-10 CNN improvement is described qualitatively, while reported numeric training-accuracy comparisons are for fully connected networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The MNIST CNN achieves 98.36% accuracy, with no identified evaluation split or numerical baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The specified CNN attains high accuracy on MNIST after the reported training period.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2021), PMLR Volume 130
record.problems: Training metrics are reported for early epochs only and do not establish zero training error. Some reported numbers are not tied to a specific epoch in the supplied text; CNN results are mainly presented as figures. The 98.36% accuracy is not identified as train or test accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The paper includes additional numerical loss and test-accuracy comparisons, but these do not directly measure training classification error or the initialization-related training accuracy emphasized by the mapped versions.

untested.parts: Eventual zero or near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, and systematic size, stopping-time or regularization comparisons.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies and extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depth with and without identity shortcuts, and the specified tanh or Fixup exceptions.

Maximum trainable depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, very deep tanh networks and 10,000-layer convolutional training. The experiments compare fixed-depth early learning rather than depth limits.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, curvature trajectories and edge-of-stability training.
Batch-normalization comparisons, higher-learning-rate tolerance and Fixup training.

missing.what: Leaky ReLU CIFAR-10 training-accuracy comparison: proposed 34.9%, Kaiming 33.36%, Xavier 10.29%; report the corresponding initialization and architecture ambiguity.
Linear CIFAR-10 training-accuracy comparison: proposed 47.87%, Kaiming 46.82%, Randwalk 47.43%, Xavier 46.92%.
Twenty-layer Leaky ReLU MNIST training-accuracy comparison: proposed 91.78%, Kaiming 91.4%, Xavier 11.63%.
Thirty-layer linear MNIST training-accuracy comparison: proposed 86.16%, Kaiming 85.53%, Randwalk 86.29%, Xavier 85.71%; this captures the comparator-dependent result.
Qualitative MNIST CNN initialization comparison: authors report improvement over Kaiming, especially during the first 30 epochs. Record separately from the unclassified 98.36% accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Early subperfect accuracy is not evidence limiting V1 without the relevant architecture, capacity and training-duration test. Figure images are absent from the supplied text, so qualitative CNN verdicts rely on the authors' explicit descriptions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, longer training beyond the reported early epochs, or systematically compare model sizes and early stopping.
Does not compare orthogonal with Gaussian weights, train very deep plain tanh networks, or test 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
